belts_chains.belt_length.title: Exact open-belt length between two pulleys

procedure.python:
def _belt_length(values):
    """Exact open-belt length (no small-angle approximation), D2 >= D1.

    alpha = asin((D2 - D1)/(2C)); wrap theta_s = pi - 2 alpha (small), theta_l = pi + 2 alpha (large).
    L = sqrt(4 C^2 - (D2 - D1)^2) + (D2 theta_l + D1 theta_s)/2.
    """
    C, D1, D2 = values['C'], values['D1'], values['D2']
    if C <= 0 or D1 <= 0 or D2 <= 0:
        raise MechError('C, D1, D2 must be positive')
    if 2 * C < abs(D2 - D1):
        raise MechError('center distance too small: need C >= (D2 - D1)/2 for an open belt')
    alpha = math.asin((D2 - D1) / (2.0 * C))
    theta_s = PI - 2.0 * alpha
    theta_l = PI + 2.0 * alpha
    L = math.sqrt(4.0 * C * C - (D2 - D1) ** 2) + (D2 * theta_l + D1 * theta_s) / 2.0
    return {'L': L}

assumptions: Open (uncrossed) belt on two pulleys, exact: alpha = asin((D2-D1)/(2C)), wrap theta_s = pi - 2 alpha (small pulley), theta_l = pi + 2 alpha (large pulley), L = sqrt(4 C^2 - (D2-D1)^2) + (D2 theta_l + D1 theta_s)/2. Requires C >= (D2-D1)/2. The familiar approximation L = 2C + pi(D1+D2)/2 + (D2-D1)^2/(4C) agrees to within ~1% for C >> (D2-D1).
method_references: Open-belt length L = sqrt(4C^2 - (D2-D1)^2) + (D2 theta_l + D1 theta_s)/2 (recalled)

belts_chains.belt_wrap.title: Angle of wrap on each pulley (open belt)

variables.name: theta_s
variables.desc: wrap angle on the small pulley
variables.label: θs

variables.name: theta_l
variables.desc: wrap angle on the large pulley
variables.label: θl

assumptions: Open belt, D2 >= D1. The small-pulley wrap angle governs friction capacity: use it in the capstan ratio (statics.belt_friction or belt_tension_ratio here). Requires C >= (D2 - D1)/2.

belts_chains.belt_centrifugal_tension.title: Centrifugal belt tension (T_c = m v^2)
assumptions: Centrifugal tension is uniform around the belt and does not contribute to power transmission; it raises the total belt tension and reduces the useful friction.

belts_chains.belt_tension_ratio.title: Belt tension ratio with centrifugal tension (capstan + T_c)

variables.name: mu
variables.desc: coefficient of friction between belt and pulley
variables.label: μ

assumptions: Impending slip on the effective tensions (total minus centrifugal): (T1 - T_c) = (T2 - T_c) e^(mu theta); a MechError is raised if T2 <= T_c (the slack-side effective tension must stay positive). With T_c = 0 this reduces to the capstan equation (statics.belt_friction). For a V-belt use the effective friction mu/sin(beta/2) (statics.vbelt_friction).

belts_chains.belt_initial_tension.title: Initial (installation) belt tension from running tensions
assumptions: T1 and T2 are the TOTAL (running) tensions; the installed tension is the mean of the effective tensions, T_i = (T1 + T2)/2 - T_c. Tension the belt so the effective tensions stay positive (T2 > T_c).

belts_chains.belt_power.title: Power transmitted by a belt (P = (T1 - T2) v)
assumptions: Centrifugal tension cancels in the difference: power is carried by (T1 - T2) alone.

belts_chains.belt_slip.title: Belt slip fraction from the speed ratio

variables.name: n1
variables.desc: driver pulley speed in rev/s (enter rpm/60)

variables.name: n2
variables.desc: driven pulley speed in rev/s (enter rpm/60)

assumptions: s = 1 - (n2 D2)/(n1 D1) = (v_driver - v_driven)/v_driver. Flat/vee belts creep ~1-2%; larger s means the belt is slipping and losing power.

belts_chains.v_belt_selection.title: V-belt design power and number of belts

variables.name: P_d
variables.desc: design power (service factor x transmitted power)

variables.name: N_b
variables.desc: number of belts (round up to an integer)

variables.name: P_r
variables.desc: rated power per belt (manufacturer catalogue input)

assumptions: P_r, K_s, C_theta and C_L are catalogue inputs. Round N_b up to the next whole belt; each belt shares the load only approximately (small drives use 1 belt).
method_references: Number of belts N_b = P_d / (P_r C_theta C_L) (recalled)

belts_chains.chain_length.title: Roller-chain length, number of links and velocity-independent length

variables.name: L_links
variables.desc: number of links (rounded up to an even integer)

procedure.python:
def _chain_length(values):
    """Roller-chain length from center distance C_p (pitches), pitch p, sprocket teeth N1, N2.

    L_p = 2 C_p + (N1 + N2)/2 + (N2 - N1)^2 / (4 pi^2 C_p)   (pitches)
    Number of links is rounded up to the nearest EVEN integer; chain length L = L_p p.
    """
    Cp, p = values['C_p'], values['p']
    N1, N2 = values['N1'], values['N2']
    if abs(N1 - round(N1)) > 1e-6 or abs(N2 - round(N2)) > 1e-6:
        raise MechError('N1 and N2 (sprocket teeth) must be integers')
    N1, N2 = int(round(N1)), int(round(N2))
    if Cp <= 0 or p <= 0:
        raise MechError('C_p (center distance in pitches) and p (pitch) must be positive')
    Lp = 2.0 * Cp + (N1 + N2) / 2.0 + (N2 - N1) ** 2 / (4.0 * PI ** 2 * Cp)
    links = int(math.ceil(Lp / 2.0)) * 2
    return {'L': Lp * p, 'L_p': Lp, 'L_links': float(links)}

assumptions: L_p = 2 C_p + (N1+N2)/2 + (N2-N1)^2/(4 pi^2 C_p). The number of links must be an even integer so the chain can be joined (offset link otherwise); it is rounded up here. Prefer ~30-50 pitches of center distance and N1 >= 17 for smooth running.
method_references: Roller-chain length in pitches (ANSI/ASME B29; recalled)

belts_chains.chain_velocity.title: Roller-chain velocity (v = p N n)
assumptions: Average chain velocity (ignores the chordal oscillation — see chordal_speed).
method_references: Chain velocity v = p N n (recalled)

belts_chains.chordal_speed.title: Chordal speed variation of a chain drive (polygon effect)

variables.name: delta_v
variables.desc: chordal speed variation, delta_v/V (fraction of the mean speed V)

assumptions: The chain rides the sprocket as a polygon, so its speed oscillates about the mean V = p N n. Shigley measures the variation relative to that mean speed: delta_v/V = (pi/N)(1/sin(pi/N) - 1/tan(pi/N)). N = 17 -> 0.0171 (1.7%), N = 6 -> 0.140 (14%). More teeth (N >= 17, preferably 19-25) reduce the variation and its whip/whine.

belts_chains.rope_working_load.title: Wire-rope safe working load (F_work = F_break / n)

variables.name: F_break
variables.desc: catalogue breaking strength of the rope

variables.name: n
variables.desc: factor of safety (design-code input; ~5 hoisting, 8-12 elevators)

assumptions: F_break is the catalogue (nominal) breaking strength; n is the design-code factor of safety. Check the bending and bearing limits too (rope_bending_stress, rope_pressure).
method_references: Safe working load = breaking strength / factor of safety (recalled)

belts_chains.rope_bending_stress.title: Wire-rope bending stress over a sheave (sigma_b = E_r d_w / D)

variables.name: sigma_b
variables.desc: bending stress in the outer wires
variables.label: σb

variables.name: E_r
variables.desc: rope modulus of elasticity (input; ~80-90 GPa for wire rope)

assumptions: Bending stress is proportional to the wire diameter over the sheave diameter — the reason large D/d_w ratios are required for long rope life (D/d >= 40 typical). E_r is an input (rope construction dependent).
method_references: Wire-rope bending stress sigma_b = E_r d_w / D (recalled)

belts_chains.rope_pressure.title: Wire-rope sheave pressure and p/Su ratio (feeds the fatigue chart)

variables.name: p
variables.desc: bearing pressure between rope and sheave

variables.name: r
variables.desc: pressure ratio p/Su (x-axis of the rope fatigue chart)

assumptions: p = 2 T/(d D) is the contact pressure of the rope on the sheave. The ratio p/Su is the abscissa of the rope maker's fatigue (bending-cycle) chart; the cycles-to-failure are read from that chart (input data, not built in).

source.derivation: Inverse: with D1 = 0.2, D2 = 0.5 the exact length is monotonic in C (for C >= 0.15 m); L = 5.11081 m is the value at C = 2 m
Inverse: L_p = 94.9761 pitches; solve 2 C_p + 34 + 29.2818/C_p = 94.9761 -> 2 C_p^2 - 60.9761 C_p + 29.2818 = 0 -> C_p = 30 (the other root 0.488 is discarded by the nearest-to-typical choice)
